title: Informal conjecture on MIS approximability vs. Min Dominating Set
statement_text: Max Independent Set may have a very different approximability status than Min Dominating Set on bounded twin-width graphs.
context_text: Twin-width: a graph has twin-width at most $d$ if it can be reduced to a single vertex by successively contracting two vertices into one, where edges from the merged vertex to vertices adjacent to only part of it become 'red', so that every intermediate graph has red degree at most $d$; such a contraction sequence is a $d$-sequence, and bounded twin-width classes include planar graphs, bounded tree-width or clique-width graphs, and proper minor-closed classes. Max Independent Set (MIS) is Distance-$1$ MIS; Distance-$r$ MIS asks for a largest set of vertices pairwise at distance at least $r$; Min $r$-Dominating Set asks for a smallest set within distance $r$ of every vertex. The authors show that, when an $O(1)$-sequence is given, Min Dominating Set, Distance-$2$ MIS and more generally Min $r$-Dominating Set and Distance-$2r$ MIS admit polynomial-time $O(1)$-approximations, as bounded twin-width implies a constant integrality gap between packing and hitting for the corresponding hypergraphs; this does not cover MIS. Their evidence that MIS behaves differently: the self-improving reduction of Feige et al. preserves twin-width, so a constant-factor approximation for MIS on graphs of twin-width at most $d$ would yield a PTAS; MIS can be $O(1)$-approximated on $K_t$-free graphs of bounded twin-width, but not obviously when the clique number is unbounded. In contrast, on general graphs Min Dominating Set cannot be approximated within $(1-o(1))\ln n$ unless P$=$NP.
